summary: Reproduced that health_generate returned 503 after a stalled probe without sending a scheduler-side abort. The timeout path now aborts the still-tracked probe before removing local state, and the scheduler busy-path now distinguishes tokenized health probes from AbortReq messages carrying the same RID prefix.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before reproduction: timeout returned 503 but the fake tokenizer manager recorded zero abort calls (expected one). Raw output: reports/j-ea9e63f332a4/evidence/failing_before_health_abort.txt

Passing-after regression and boundaries: one abort on timeout while state is tracked, no abort on success, generate and embedding probe recognition, ordinary RID rejection, and AbortReq exclusion. Result: 5 passed. Raw output: reports/j-ea9e63f332a4/evidence/passing_after_focused_tests.txt
Repository formatting, lint, syntax, test registration, and policy hooks for all changed implementation and test files.

gpu_execution.evidence: No GPU execution was used. The defect and correction are HTTP/tokenizer/scheduler control-flow and IPC message classification; the prepared gfx950 cannot reproduce the reported NVIDIA Qwen3.8/NEXTN paged-prefill crash.

remaining_limitations: The reported Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 NEXTN workload and NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell hardware/weights were unavailable, so the downstream paged-prefill shape-mismatch crash was not reproduced or claimed fixed.

Validation deterministically covers dispatch of the explicit scheduler abort and prevention of that AbortReq being filtered as a busy health probe; it does not claim a full-model or multi-node reproduction.
The separate GPU reset-required failure described by the reporter was not investigated.
